Typically, when using it, the front will be facing and close to the bench, so tipping forwards is not a huge issue. The curved legs are to put the back legs as far out as is practical so that it's hard to tip backwards.

I made this stool so that my son (a little over a year old when I finished it) could see what we were doing on the bench and will eventually be able to help with cooking and learn etc.

It's made almost entirely out of some scrap construction lumber (all hardwood, probably Messmate) that came out of my house when we had some windows replaced.

There are no nails or screws used, the only metal is two 1/4" coach bolts that are used to secure the adjustable top step in place. The joinery is predominantly mortise and tenon with wedged through mortises visible on the side frame. Since I was using reclaimed timber, there were quite a few nail holes etc in the wood. Some of these I just didn't worry about, but the ones on the surfaces that were likely to get touched or dirty I filled by driving in small wooden dowels then planing them flush.

The back leg is curved in a ~2' radius. This was done by ripping the stock into thin strips (each a bit less than 1/4") and gluing them up in a jig.
